items.stem: A web tier must handle sudden, unpredictable spikes in traffic while keeping costs aligned to demand. Which approach best fits a resilient, cost-aware AWS design?

options.text: Auto-scaling compute behind a load balancer across multiple Availability Zones
options.rationale: Correct: auto scaling across AZs behind a load balancer gives elasticity, resilience and demand-aligned cost.

options.text: A single large server running continuously at peak size
options.rationale: A single fixed server is neither resilient nor cost-aligned to variable demand.

options.text: Manually launching servers when users complain
options.rationale: Manual, reactive scaling is slow and unreliable.

options.text: Disabling health checks to save effort

items.explanation: Correct: auto scaling across AZs behind a load balancer gives elasticity, resilience and demand-aligned cost.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which practice best protects sensitive data at rest in an AWS storage service?

options.text: Enabling encryption at rest using managed keys
options.rationale: Correct: encryption at rest with managed keys protects stored data.
Public access exposes data and is the opposite of protection.
Removing logging reduces visibility and does not protect data.

options.text: Storing credentials in plaintext in the app
options.rationale: Plaintext credentials are a serious security risk.

items.explanation: Correct: encryption at rest with managed keys protects stored data.

items.stem: Select TWO design choices that improve the resilience of an AWS architecture. (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: multi-AZ deployment increases fault tolerance.

options.text: Decoupling components with a managed queue
options.rationale: Correct: decoupling with a queue isolates failures and improves resilience.

options.text: Hardcoding a single server's IP everywhere
options.rationale: Hardcoding one server is a single point of failure.

options.text: Running everything in one subnet with no redundancy

items.explanation: Correct: multi-AZ deployment increases fault tolerance.
